value.built_to: decide propositional satisfiability of large CNF formulas and, when satisfiable, produce a model
value.pressure: industrial verification instances with millions of clauses; the need for a small, readable, extensible solver others could build on
value.success_means: correct SAT/UNSAT answers (models checkable, UNSAT trusted or proof-logged) fast on competition and industrial benchmarks

ANCESTRY.value: MiniSat (2003-2010, Chalmers; Niklas Een, Niklas Sorensson): minimal CDCL SAT solver with two-watched literals, VSIDS, conflict-clause learning and restarts; the reference from which most modern SAT solvers descend

cut.note: conflict-driven clause learning in 900 lines: unit propagation over two watched literals per clause (with a cached 'blocker' literal to skip clause reads), first-UIP conflict analysis producing one learnt clause with a backjump level, activity-ordered decisions (VSIDS) with decay implemented by growing the increment, learnt-clause deletion by activity with binary and reason clauses protected, and Luby-sequence restarts; each of the five is a separately replaceable policy and each was later replaced by descendants

organs.human_name: propagate (449-524): watches[p], Watcher{cref, blocker}, the false literal forced into c[1], the search for a new watch from k = 2, unit -> uncheckedEnqueue, conflict -> stop and copy remaining watches
organs.mechanism: for each newly false literal p, scan the clauses watching ~p: if the watcher's cached blocker literal is true skip without reading the clause; otherwise ensure the false literal is in position 1, if position 0 is true keep the watch, else look for another non-false literal from position 2 on and move the watch there; if none exists the clause is unit (enqueue position 0 with this clause as reason) or conflicting (return it, having copied the remaining watchers); watches are never touched on backtracking
organs.output: new assignments or a conflict clause
organs.state: watch lists per literal; the trail; qhead
assumptions: two watches suffice to detect unit and conflict, and need no undo (Moskewicz et al. 2001); a cheap cached literal makes most watcher visits cost one lookup
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: propagation cost independent of clause length and of backtracking
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the watcher lists are shrunk in place (a stable partition), so a long list with many satisfied clauses is still scanned; that is what the blocker mitigates
organs.human_prior: Chaff's two-literal watching (2001); the blocker literal is MiniSat 2.2's own

organs.human_name: analyze (264-360): seen[], pathC, the reason chain via reason(var(p)), out_learnt[0] = ~p; ccmin_mode 2 with abstractLevel and litRedundant; out_btlevel from the max level among the rest
organs.mechanism: starting from the conflict clause, mark its literals; literals from the current decision level are counted (pathC), older ones go into the learnt clause; walk the trail backwards to the most recent marked literal, resolve with its reason clause, repeat until exactly one current-level literal remains (the first unique implication point), which negated becomes the asserting literal; then remove literals implied by others in the clause (recursive redundancy check with a level bitmask as a fast filter); the backjump level is the highest level among the remaining literals, so the learnt clause is unit there
organs.input: a conflict clause; the trail; reasons
organs.output: a learnt clause and a backtrack level
assumptions: the first UIP gives short, quickly asserting clauses (empirically better than later cuts); minimisation pays for itself
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: every conflict yields a clause that forces a new assignment immediately after backjumping (non-chronological); the search never repeats the same failure
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the learnt clause length is unbounded; the DB reduction exists because of it
organs.human_prior: GRASP (Marques-Silva & Sakallah 1996) for learning; Chaff for first UIP; Sorensson & Biere 2009 for minimisation

organs.human_name: pickBranchLit (225-240): random_var_freq, order_heap.removeMin, polarity[]; Solver.h varBumpActivity / varDecayActivity (var_inc *= 1/var_decay; rescale at 1e100); analyze bumps every variable it sees
organs.mechanism: each variable carries an activity; every variable touched during conflict analysis is bumped by the current increment; instead of decaying all activities after each conflict the increment itself grows by 1/var_decay (rescaling everything when it overflows), which is the same ordering at O(1) cost; decisions pop the maximum-activity unassigned variable from a heap, with a small probability of a random variable instead; the literal's sign comes from the polarity vector
assumptions: variables recently involved in conflicts are the ones worth deciding on (locality of conflicts); recency should dominate frequency, hence exponential decay
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a decision heuristic that costs O(log n) per decision and adapts to the search
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with var_decay near 1 the heuristic becomes frequency-based and stale; the random picks exist to escape
organs.human_prior: Chaff's VSIDS (2001); the increment-growth trick is MiniSat's (Een & Sorensson 2003)

organs.human_name: reduceDB (525-545) with reduceDB_lt; search: learnts.size() - nAssigns() >= max_learnts; max_learnts *= learntsize_inc on the learntsize_adjust schedule; claBumpActivity / claDecayActivity
organs.mechanism: learnt clauses carry an activity bumped when they take part in a conflict; when the number of learnt clauses beyond the current assignment exceeds max_learnts, sort by activity (binary clauses last), delete the lower-activity half plus any below a threshold, never deleting binary clauses or clauses that are the reason for a current assignment; the limit starts at a fraction of the original clause count and grows geometrically on a schedule keyed to conflict counts
assumptions: most learnt clauses stop being useful; recent usefulness (activity) predicts future usefulness; the database may grow slowly forever
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: propagation stays fast as learning continues
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: activity is a poor proxy on some families (LBD replaced it in Glucose, 2009)
organs.human_prior: Chaff's deletion; the activity-based halving is MiniSat's

organs.human_name: solve_ (751-790): rest_base = luby(restart_inc, curr_restarts) or restart_inc^k; search(rest_base * restart_first); luby (734-743)
organs.mechanism: the search runs until a conflict budget is spent, then backtracks to level 0 (keeping every learnt clause and all activities) and starts again with a budget that follows the Luby sequence (1,1,2,1,1,2,4,...) times a base of 100 conflicts, or a geometric sequence if configured; because the state that matters (clauses, activities, polarities) survives, a restart is a re-ordering of decisions, not a fresh start
assumptions: run-time distributions of CDCL are heavy-tailed, so restarting with a universal (Luby) schedule bounds the expected time within a log factor of the optimal fixed cutoff (Luby, Sinclair, Zuckerman 1993)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: escapes from unlucky early decisions at no loss of learnt information
organs.human_prior: Gomes et al. 1998 (restarts for heavy tails); Huang 2007 (Luby in SAT)

pressures.source_evidence: Solver.cc propagate, analyze, pickBranchLit, reduceDB, solve_
pressures.condition: an organism searches assignments for a CNF with millions of clauses; a wrong early decision can cost the whole budget; the same sub-failures recur across branches; propagation must be cheap per assignment
pressures.failure_condition: timeouts on instances solvable by learning and restarts; propagation cost growing with clause length or with backtracking; a learnt database that starves propagation
pressures.world_punishes: chronological backtracking without learning; counting-based propagation; fixed decision orders; no restarts; unbounded learning
pressures.world_rewards: watched literals, first-UIP learning with backjumping, activity-based decisions, bounded learnt sets, restart schedules
pressures.observable_consequence: instances solved within a time budget on a standard set (SAT competition families) with each policy replaced by its naive predecessor one at a time
pressures.vacuity_condition: 2-SAT or Horn instances (linear time without any of this)
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: instances with a planted solution and a known assignment (the world withholds it)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the satisfying assignment must verify it in one propagation pass; DPLL without learning must fail the pigeonhole and industrial families where CDCL succeeds; CDCL without restarts must show the heavy tail across seeds: the world must show all three
